title: Erdős-Hajnal Conjecture
statement_text: For every graph $H$, there exists $\tau > 0$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\max(\alpha(G), \omega(G)) \geq |G|^\tau$.
context_text: The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for proper hereditary graph classes, the largest clique or stable set is guaranteed to have polynomial (rather than merely logarithmic) size. Prior to this paper it was known for $K_2$, $P_4$, the bull, and their closures under complements and substitution, but remained open for $C_5$, $P_5$, and $\overline{P_5}$ among graphs on five vertices.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for $H = C_5$: every $C_5$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\max(\alpha(G), \omega(G)) \geq |G|^\tau$ for some absolute constant $\tau > 0$.

title: Erdős-Hajnal property for $\{C_8, \overline{C_8}\}$
context_text: A graph $G$ is $\mathcal{H}$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{H}$; $\overline{H}$ denotes the complement of $H$ and $|G|$ the number of vertices. A set $\mathcal{H}$ of graphs has the Erdős–Hajnal property if there exists $\tau>0$ such that $\max(\alpha(G),\omega(G))\ge|G|^\tau$ for every $\mathcal{H}$-free graph $G$; the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture asserts that every single graph has it. Excluding both $C_8$ and $\overline{C_8}$ is a stronger restriction than excluding $C_8$ alone, so the question is a weakening of the conjecture for $C_8$. The paper's main result is that $C_5$ has the Erdős–Hajnal property; with the same method the authors also prove that $\{C_6,\overline{C_6}\}$ and $\{C_7,\overline{C_7}\}$ have it, that $\{C,\overline{H}\}$ has it for every cycle $C$ and forest $H$, and that a cycle together with the complements of all cycles of length at least $\ell$ has it. They remark that it would be nice to know whether $\{C_8,\overline{C_8}\}$ has the property, but this remains open.
notes: Stated in running prose as 'it would be nice to know if the same is true for $\{C_8,\overline{C_8}\}$, but this remains open'; no formal theorem environment.
